items.title: incrementalJoin can only JOIN an existing community, never CREATE one; novel-neighbourhood episodes are permanently excluded

rootCause.evidence: Steady-state wiring: the periodic enrich tick resolves fullPass ONLY from a pending memory_curate recluster trigger (`hasPendingFullEnrich`, extensions/bundles/sox-memory-bundle/members/memory-server/src/index.ts:2382-2383) and otherwise always runs `runEnrichIsolated(dbPath, { incrementalCluster: !fullPass }, ...)` (index.ts:2389-2391) — so in steady state EVERY pass is incremental. On that path `clusterStore` → `computeClusters` takes the incremental branch (libs/memory-core/src/cluster.ts:1016 `isFullPass = !opts.incrementalOnly && count <= nodeCap`; :894-914) and calls `incrementalJoin` (cluster.ts:645-870), which (a) returns `joined:0` via the `no_target` early return when no live community exists in scope (cluster.ts:682-689) or none has a member vector (cluster.ts:714-720), and (b) for every candidate whose best single-link similarity to ANY existing member is below tau, `continue`s into `rejected_below_threshold` (cluster.ts:787-797) — candidates are never grouped among themselves. The incremental branch returns `clusters: []` (cluster.ts:907-913), so the materialize guard `if (result.clusters.length > 0)` (cluster.ts:1036) never fires and `materializeClusters` never runs on the incremental path; communities are born ONLY in full/subset passes (computeClusters full branch → runClusters/buildClusterResults, cluster.ts:959-972). This is the current mechanism after the BL-496 merge (ddd3fa08, in main, changed the rejection path from a bare `{joined:0}` to the `emptyAdmission` + `recordJoinOutcome('no_target')` instrumentation at cluster.ts:656-665/682-689/714-720 — re-derived, not inherited). The H2 population is documented as permanent at cluster-metrics.ts:169-175 ('the same episode is re-rejected on every subsequent tick, forever').

testPlan.name: BL-495 regression: incrementalJoin CREATES a community for a mutually-similar novel neighbourhood when no community target exists
testPlan.assertion: Fresh store, write 3 mutually-similar ≥50-char episodes (the existing GROUP_A_CONTENT fixture), NO full pass, then `runBatchEnrich({ incrementalCluster: true })` → `incResult.communities_upserted >= 1`, `(await clusterStats(adapter)).cluster_count >= 1`, `total_clustered >= 2`, and the persisted community uid equals a locally recomputed sha256 of the sorted member rowids (deterministic minting).
testPlan.whyCatches: Pre-fix the no_target early return (cluster.ts:682-689) yields joined:0/communities_upserted:0 for exactly this shape — the orphan-forever defect. Post-fix the ≥τ group is minted. Second companion test ('two novel episodes with a ≥τ partner join each other into a NEW community despite being below τ against every existing community') covers the measured 94-orphan signature: seed one community + full pass, write 2 mutually-similar novel episodes, incremental pass → both end MEMBER_OF one NEW community (community_count +1). Pre-fix both stay rejected_below_threshold (cluster.ts:787-797). REQUIRED same-commit revisions: cluster-incremental-join.spec.ts:125 (`communities_upserted === 0` in incremental mode), :146-168 (empty-community-table deferral test), and enrich.spec.ts:973-1000 ('no communities written') — each asserts the defect as a feature and must be flipped in the same change; the enrich.spec.ts test is itself a ready-made pre-fix oracle.

items.title: incremental join never updates meta.member_count (or the member-set-hash community_uid); memory_get_community under-reports members and the next full pass mints a different uid

rootCause.evidence: The join loop writes ONLY the MEMBER_OF edge (cluster.ts:817-822 `INSERT INTO edge ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE SET t_invalid = NULL`) and never touches the community node's meta. meta.member_count is written in exactly one place, materializeClusters (cluster.ts:460-465, `member_count: cluster.member_rowids.length`), which runs only on full/subset passes — so between full passes the stored count is stale by exactly the number of incremental joins. The read side consumes that stale value: memory_get_community parses meta.member_count (index.ts:1759-1761) and the fallback `if (memberCount === 0) memberCount = members.length` (index.ts:1775) only fires when meta says 0, NOT when it is stale-but-nonzero — so a community that grew 2→3 incrementally reports `member_count: 2` beside a 3-row `members` array. The uid consequence: communityUid is a pure hash of the member set (cluster.ts:265-268), so any membership growth re-mints the uid at the next full pass, orphaning the pre-join uid (materializeClusters invalidate-then-insert, cluster.ts:417-443, 467-493; churn visible via the revived/created counters, cluster-metrics.ts:528-538). Constraint status: the 'do not land before BL-496 deploys' constraint is CLEAR — the BL-496 censoring filter reads live edges, not meta (cluster-metrics.ts:354-367 `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM edge e ...)` with CLUSTER_ELIGIBLE_SQL), so updating meta.member_count at join time cannot corrupt the historical join-rate record. BL-496 code is merged in main (ddd3fa08; cluster-metrics.ts censoring filter at :361; bl496-time-to-community.spec.ts present).
unverified: The specific live artifact sha 6eff093e3991 is NOT an ancestor of main (BL-496 code reached main via merge ddd3fa08). The artifact-sha identity is a deployment record outside the repo — BL-496 code presence in the tree is confirmed, the exact deployed sha is not.

functions: incrementalJoin (cluster.ts:645) — after the join loop, for each community that gained members this pass, `UPDATE node SET meta = json_set(meta, '$.member_count', <communityLiveMemberCount + joinedThisPass>) WHERE rowid = ?` (one UPDATE per touched community; json_set preserves cluster_scope/mean_intra_sim). Deliberately NOT a read-modify-write of the full blob.
fixSurface.shape: Write-side only. Do NOT touch the memory_get_community read side (index.ts:1755-1775) — that region is being edited by the in-flight feat/bug-memory-006 branch; the write-side fix makes the read side correct with zero index.ts contention. The uid is NOT recomputed at join (re-keying the community node mid-tick would orphan every reference; uid stability between full passes is by design — cluster.ts:257-268 and the revived-vs-created accounting, cluster-metrics.ts:528-538). 'Recompute community_uid' in the defect text resolves to the BL-495 CREATE path's deterministic minting, which is BL-495's surface, not this one.

testPlan.name: BUG-MEMORY-010 regression: after incrementalJoin adds a member, community meta.member_count equals the live MEMBER_OF edge count
testPlan.assertion: Seed a 2-member community via full pass; write a 3rd mutually-similar episode; `runBatchEnrich({ incrementalCluster: true })`; then read the community node's meta and assert `JSON.parse(meta).member_count === 3 === (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM edge WHERE dst = <community rowid> AND rel='MEMBER_OF' AND t_invalid IS NULL)`. Optionally assert end-to-end: memory_get_community returns `community.member_count === members.length`.
testPlan.whyCatches: Pre-fix the join loop writes the edge (cluster.ts:817-822) and never the meta, so the stored member_count stays 2 — and the read-side fallback (index.ts:1775) only rescues the 0 case, so the response is internally inconsistent (member_count 2, members 3). The assertion pins meta.member_count to the live edge count — exactly the invariant the defect violates. Keeping the assertion in libs/memory-core (meta level) makes the memory-server handler a non-gate for this fix.

items.title: selectEpisodes silently excludes episodes with content < 50 chars (undocumented arbitrary floor excludes real content by 3 chars)

rootCause.evidence: The floor is the exported constant `CLUSTER_MIN_CONTENT_LENGTH = 50` (cluster.ts:57), embedded in `CLUSTER_ELIGIBLE_SQL` (`LENGTH(n.content) >= ${CLUSTER_MIN_CONTENT_LENGTH}`, cluster.ts:60-61), which is aliased as `EPISODE_CANDIDATE_PREDICATE` (cluster.ts:74) and consumed verbatim by `selectEpisodes` (cluster.ts:556-569) — so any episode with content length 1..49 is structurally excluded from clustering input and from every metrics census that shares the constant: ineligible/awaiting_vector/awaiting_or_rejected (cluster-metrics.ts:317/323/329) and the ever_clustered_fraction regime query (:361). A 47-char episode is excluded 'by 3 chars'. The floor is documented as a spec invariant (D5.1 comment at cluster.ts:10, and cluster-metrics.ts:112 'a permanent, by-design exclusion') but has no recorded rationale beyond being a guard against degenerate short-content clusters; the bl496 spec pins the boundary (bl496-time-to-community.spec.ts:314, :339 construct sub-50 episodes as 'ineligible BY DESIGN').
unverified: Whether the floor exists for anti-percolation (short near-duplicate fragments cluster trivially tightly) or for cost is not recorded anywhere in code or the findings doc — the 'arbitrary' characterization is the task's, consistent with the absence of a rationale citation.

fixSurface.shape: Minimal fix = lower the constant (e.g. 20) or make it env-configurable with a lower default. Do NOT remove the floor to 0: `LENGTH('') >= 0` admits empty-string episodes (no vector → they land in the metrics' awaiting_vector bucket forever — noise) and the anti-percolation value of SOME floor remains unexamined. Changing the value is the only shape that keeps the selectEpisodes/metrics lockstep invariant intact.

testPlan.name: BL-497 regression: an episode with content length in [newFloor, 50) is a clustering candidate and joins a community
testPlan.assertion: Write an episode whose content is ~47 chars sharing vocabulary with an existing seeded community; `runBatchEnrich({ incrementalCluster: true })`; assert the episode gains a live MEMBER_OF edge and `clusterStats().total_clustered` increases by 1. Companion assertion: the bl496-time-to-community.spec.ts ineligible-boundary fixtures (:314, :339) are re-based to the new floor so the metrics census stays consistent with the new predicate.
testPlan.whyCatches: The single predicate constant (cluster.ts:60-61) is the ONLY gate between an episode and selectEpisodes (cluster.ts:556-569). Pre-fix, a 47-char episode is invisible to every pass and every census bucket — the test's write is simply never considered, so total_clustered does not move. Post-fix it joins. It also guards the lockstep invariant: if someone later changes the value in only one place, either the clustering input or the metrics census silently diverges, and this test (clustering side) plus the re-based bl496 fixtures (metrics side) catch it.

The branch's new E_PENDING_CLUSTER error (entity_uid path, index.ts:1750-1757 on the branch) is the read-path counterpart of BL-495's orphan population. After BL-495 lands, genuinely-novel-neighbourhood episodes resolve instead of staying pending forever — the branch's spec seeds a genuinely-unclustered episode and its E_PENDING_CLUSTER pin stays valid (just rarer). If Packet A merges first, the branch's spec must ensure its seeded 'unclustered' episode has no ≥τ partner, or the pin may see the episode become clustered.

The branch's D8 rule (commit 7a914675 'defer reclustering-superseded community_uid') documents exactly the uid-churn phenomenon BUG-MEMORY-010 observes. BL-495's CREATE must mint uids via the same communityUid(salt) the full pass uses, so D8's deferral semantics stay coherent.

If Packet A merges first, the branch's E_PENDING_CLUSTER spec author should re-check the 'unclustered episode' fixture as noted.
